Learn from the call

Academy

Follow a real call from the original moment to the chart and the lesson. Five case studies show what was said and what happened next.

How these case studies are built

Each case identifies its chart source. Some charts are reconstructions for teaching; others use dated market prices. No exit is inferred and no P&L is scored.

Entry
Invalidation

01 The setup
02 Reading the chart
Entry is where the desk got in. Invalidation is the level that proves the thesis wrong. Target is a reference level discussed in the setup, not an inferred exit. If price crosses invalidation, the trade is over, no debate.

Kenny @KtheQuant
Degen & on-chain analyst · editorial operator behind The Record

Five years across crypto, equities and commodities. I built The Record's pipeline, write the Dispatch for each edition, and curate its Lexicon from the tape. Before the show: the research. During: the read. After: the memory.

The Desk is written by Kenny (@KtheQuant). Reads are framed to be argued with, not taken as investment advice. The level that invalidates each thesis comes first, because a call without an exit is just a vibe. Kenny · @KtheQuant
